segments.narration: Sixty people were left on a sandbank for fifteen years. No trees, no fresh water, and a promise someone would come back.
The Utile was a French slave ship. She struck this island in July 1761, carrying Malagasy captives illegally.
The crew built a boat from the wreck. In September, 122 Frenchmen sailed off and left everyone else on the sand.
Mauritius refused to send a ship. There was a war on. The survivors built stone shelters, kept a fire alive, and waited.
The Dauphine arrived in November 1776. Seven women and an eight-month-old baby were still there. Archaeologists have since dug out their hearths.
